script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Romance
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIBRARY - DAY

Amelia (mid-20s, bookish and shy) sits at a table, engrossed in a novel. A bell chimes, signaling the closing hour. Amelia reluctantly packs up her things.

NARRATOR (V.O.) ( Amelia's thoughts )
I can't believe the library's closing already.

EXT. LIBRARY ENTRANCE - DAY

Amelia locks the library door behind her and breathes a sigh of relief. She looks around, and her eyes land on a man, Lucas (mid-20s, good-looking and outgoing), sitting on the steps, engrossed in a sketchbook.

AMELIA
(surprised)
You're still here?

LUCAS
(looking up, smiling)
Yes, I am. I could spend hours in here.

Amelia blushes and smiles back, feeling a sudden rush of excitement.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY (2 WEEKS LATER)

Amelia and Lucas sit across from each other, sipping their coffees.

LUCAS
So, you really love reading, huh?

AMELIA
(smiling)
Yes, it's my escape from the world. What about you? Why the sketchbook?

LUCAS
(grinning)
I love to draw, especially people. I find their stories fascinating.

They share a laugh and continue their conversation, discovering more about each other.

EXT. PARK - DAY (4 WEEKS LATER)

Amelia and Lucas sit on a blanket, surrounded by a sea of blooming flowers. They've come here every week since their first chance encounter at the library. They share stories, laughs, and even silence.

AMelia
(looking up at the sky)
I can't believe how fast time has flown by. It feels like we've known each other forever.

LUCAS
(nodding)
I feel the same way. Our friendship has become my favorite story.

They share a warm smile, enjoying the moment.

INT. LIBRARY - NIGHT (1 MONTH LATER)

Amelia arrives at the library to find it closed due to a power outage. She's disappointed but not surprised. She hears a faint tapping on a nearby window. She looks out and sees Lucas, holding a lantern, tapping to get her attention.

LUCAS
(smiling)
I know you love the library, so I brought you a lantern. We can still have our weekly meeting, even if the library can't.

Amelia's heart swells with gratitude and love. They sit on the library steps, talking and sharing stories by the light of the lantern.

NARRATOR (V.O.) ( Amelia's thoughts )
Our friendship has become my favorite story, one filled with laughter, love, and the magic of the library.

FADE OUT.
